Subject: Follow-up: procurement & approvals (post discovery)

Hi Alicia & Ben,

Thanks again for taking the time today - great to learn more about Acme's ML roadmap and where Redwood could fit (low-latency inference for customer-facing features). Per our discussion, two quick recaps and asks to keep momentum: 

1) Procurement path: can you confirm whether Acme will do a PO (preferred for larger, multi-quarter commitments) vs. corporate card for initial purchases? Also: are you interested in transacting through AWS Marketplace (or similar) or direct contract?

2) Budget owners & approvers: who is the economic buyer and finance sponsor we should map to (name, role, email)? Also who is the legal/signatory for agreements?

3) Next steps: I attached a short procurement checklist and a draft SOW to accelerate internal approvals. If you can share your PO template or procurement contacts, we'll fill in the SOW and loop them into the procurement thread.

Attached: Redwood-Procurement-Checklist.xlsx, Redwood-SOW-draft.pdf

Looking forward - I can be flexible on timing next week to join any procurement sync.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Alicia Gomez <agomez@acme.com>

Date: 2026-03-30T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Follow-up: procurement & approvals (post discovery)

Hi Marissa - thanks for the clear recap. A few notes from our side after chatting with procurement: 

- Commercial path: For transactions above $100k we require a formal PO. For small pilots under $25k we typically use a corporate card. There is some flexibility around a proof-of-concept if we classify it as a partner pilot.
- Marketplace: We prefer AWS Marketplace for quick procurement, but our procurement team needs to vet marketplace contracts vs. a direct PO (they tend to prefer POs for longer commitments).
- Budget & approvers: Economic buyer is Jordan Lee (VP Engineering) - jlee@acme.com. Finance sponsor is Liam O'Connor (Director, Finance) - loconnor@acme.com. Legal/signatory for standard SaaS-like procurement is our CFO, Kristine Park (kpark@acme.com), for deals above our threshold.

I'll loop in our procurement lead if needed - they can share a PO template and expected lead times. For now, please go ahead and draft the SOW and include an estimated annual cost with token/usage tiers so finance can see the spend profile.

Thanks,
Alicia
Head of Product Partnerships
Acme Corp
agomez@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-03-31T08:45:00Z
Subject: Internal: ACME procurement mapping & recommended commercial path (deal ACME-2026-0045)

Vivek / Aditya - quick internal note after Acme's reply: 

Summary:
- They prefer a PO for >$100k, card for <$25k, marketplace optional but needs procurement approval.
- Economic buyer: Jordan Lee (VP Eng) - signatory: CFO Kristine Park - finance sponsor: Liam O'Connor.

Recommendation:
- Position: 12-month Dedicated reserved capacity as primary commercial path (predictable price and SLAs). Ask for a PO to cover the first 12 months.
- Backstop: Offer a 3-month pilot on card under $25k to accelerate momentum if procurement timing is slow.
- Marketplace: Keep as an option for procurement to expedite purchasing, but don't rely on it for initial contract language.

Next steps for us:
- Finalize SOW (I will update with PO vs Card pricing tiers and expected invoicing cadence).
- Prepare a short procurement FAQ (invoicing, tax, SLAs, data residency) for their procurement team.
- Request Acme's PO template and expected lead time.

I'll draft the SOW this afternoon and share for quick review - please flag any pricing/legal hooks we should avoid.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-04-02T09:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: ACME procurement mapping & recommended commercial path (deal ACME-2026-0045)

Agree with the approach. Two quick asks:
- When you send the updated SOW, include a line-item pricing table (Committed monthly tokens, overage rates, and what triggers autoscaling). Procurement will want clear banding.
- Please ask Acme for their PO template and the contact at procurement (so Finance can do a dry run). If they can share expected approval lead times, we can propose a parallel card-based pilot to keep momentum.

If you want, I can prep a redline-friendly template for the SOW to speed legal review.

- Vivek
